The *Nāgapupphiyattheraapadāna* is a biographical poem preserved within the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the past karmic deeds and spiritual attainment of the elder (*thera*) Nāgapupphiya. SuttaCentral lists five modern translations of the text in five languages, though no standalone English title is assigned in the database [SuttaCentral].
No direct external parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections are attested at significant match thresholds [DharmaNexus]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 46 matching passages across 16 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest partner in reuse is the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (12 matches; longest §0.3–6.4), which quotes or discusses substantial portions of the verses [DharmaNexus]. In addition, repetitive formulaic segments—most notably segments 6.3–9.1—are shared with a wide array of other devotional poems in the *Therāpadāna*, such as the *Gaṇṭhipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 131), *Punnāgapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 161 and Tha-Ap 335), *Tamālapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 193), *Pañcaṅguliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 172), and *Kiṁkaṇikapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 201) [DharmaNexus].
